paper.title: Restless-UCB, an Efficient and Low-complexity Algorithm for Online Restless Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Online restless bandit with birth-death Markov chains
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless Markov arms (environment markovian) are out of scope in ontology v0.5.
unmapped: each arm has a Markov chain on M states evolving every step regardless of pulls; reward mean depends on arm and current state
player observes the current state of the pulled arm
regret against the optimal average-reward policy with full knowledge of transitions
birth-death transitions, monotone rewards in state, P(k,k+1)+P(k+1,k)<=1, transition probabilities to neighbours >= c_1
settings.definition_quote: Consider an online restless bandit problem $\mathcal{R}$ which has one player (decision maker) and $N$ arms ... Each arm $i$ is associated with a Markov chain $M_i$ ... this action gives a reward $x(t) \in [0,1]$ ... $Reg(T) = T\mu^*(\mathcal{R}) - \sum_{t=1}^T \E[x^\pi(t)]$.

symbols.M_states: number of states of each arm's Markov chain
symbols.d_min: minimum stationary probability over arms and states
symbols.lambda_max: max over arms of sup second-largest eigenvalue modulus over a neighbourhood of transition matrices

conditions: Assumptions 1-4: rewards monotone decreasing in state index, birth-death transitions, P_i(k,k+1)+P_i(k+1,k)<=1, neighbour transition probs >= c_1
Oracle returns the exact optimal offline policy

source.label: Theorem_1
source.quote: If \texttt{Oracle} returns the optimal policy, then under Assumptions 1-4, the regret of Restless-UCB with $m(T) = T^{2\over 3}$ in an online restless bandit problem $\mathcal{R}$ satisfies: $Reg(T) = \tilde{O}\left(\left({N\over d_{\min}} + {M^3\over (1-\lambda_{\max})^2}\right)T^{2\over 3}\right)$.

results.notes: N arms mapped to K. Regret defined via expected rewards against the optimal average-reward policy. Hidden constant includes diameter-like constant C and 1/c_1^3 terms. Computation O(N) to build instance given efficient oracle.

conditions: Oracle returns an approximate policy with ratio lambda

source.label: Proposition_Approx
source.quote: If \texttt{Oracle} returns an approximate policy with ratio $\lambda$, then under Assumptions 1-4, the approximation regret (with approximate ratio $\lambda$) of Restless-UCB with $m(T) = T^{2\over 3}$ in an online restless bandit problem $\mathcal{R}$ is upper bounded by $\tilde{O}(T^{2\over 3})$.

results.notes: Hidden constant may be exponential (diameter D). Dependence labelled worst_case only in T; constants instance-dependent.
